triage_method: Every case's julia_surface text was grepped against src/*.jl and src/families/*.jl (function/struct name search); a hit was then read in full and, where the case's r_call implied a live fit, smoke-tested locally in Julia (and, for the one EXECUTABLE_NOW case, cross-checked against the maintainer's locally installed but UNPINNED gllvmTMB 0.7.1 as a syntax/sanity smoke test only -- not authoritative frozen-oracle evidence). A grep hit alone was not treated as sufficient: several cases (extract_Gamma, getLV, getLoadings, StatsAPI.fitted, extract_lv_effects, ordination) have a same-named or closely-related Julia function but fail on kwarg vocabulary (R's multi-tier `level=` argument has no GLLVM.jl equivalent -- GLLVM.jl's GllvmFit carries one undecomposed covariance, not R's unit/unit_obs/phy/... tier system), calling convention (R reads stored fit state; Julia's fitted()/getLV() require the response matrix `y` as an explicit argument), or fixture mechanism (the *-BRIDGE cases against a `gllvmTMB_julia` RCall bridge fit need the RCall/JuliaCall harness in src/bridge.jl, not a plain native-surface check) -- these were triaged NEEDS_NEW_JULIA_SURFACE with the specific gap recorded, not EXECUTABLE_NOW on symbol-name existence alone.
five_reclassified_rows_note: These 5 postfit-1.json rows carry reclassify.to='compatibility_adapter' with an empty case_specs list already in the frozen manifest draft -- they are not part of the 51-case annex and are not re-triaged here.

executable_batch.model: value ~ 0 + trait + latent(0 + trait | site, d = K, unique = FALSE), family = gaussian(), on Julia side fit_gaussian_gllvm(Y; K=K, X=X) with X the per-species dummy design (X[s,:,s]=1 for species s, matching R's ~0+trait fixed part)

fixture.fixture_provenance: Deterministic, hand-embedded (not regenerated by either runner at run time): generated once via Random.MersenneTwister(20260901) in Julia (p=4 species, n=24 sites, K=1 latent factor, true beta = [-1, -1/3, 1/3, 1]), rounded to 6 decimals, and frozen into this contract as the single source of truth for both tools/core070_postfit_1_batch.R and tools/core070_postfit_1_batch.jl. Neither runner re-derives Y from a seed -- both read it from here, so no RNG-portability assumption between R and Julia is load-bearing.
fixture.r_dataframe_construction: df <- data.frame(site = factor(rep(seq_len(n), each = p)), trait = factor(rep(paste0('t', seq_len(p)), times = n), levels = paste0('t', seq_len(p))), value = as.vector(Ymat)) where Ymat is Y reshaped to a p x n matrix in the same row=species/col=site layout as the JSON above (matrix(..., nrow=p, byrow=TRUE)); as.vector() flattens column-major (site-major, species-fastest), matching rep(seq_len(n), each=p) / rep(trait_levels, times=n).

comparands: R coef.gllvmTMB_multi(fit) named vector (traitt1..traitt4, in trait-factor level order)
Julia coef(fit_gaussian_gllvm(Y; K=K, X=X)) plain vector, species index 1..p in the same order as the trait factor levels
executable_batch.tolerance_rationale: Local smoke (this session, unpinned gllvmTMB 0.7.1, not the frozen oracle) showed R vs Julia coef() differing by <2e-6 on this exact fixture (R: -1.0058017 -0.2481031 0.3536588 0.9301411; Julia: -1.00580175 -0.2481022083 0.35365920833 0.93014141667) -- both engines recover the analytic MLE of a linear-Gaussian factor model, which has no cross-engine optimizer ambiguity for beta (unlike Lambda, beta is not subject to the latent-rotation identifiability gauge). 1e-3 leaves headroom for the frozen reference-commit build differing slightly from the locally-installed 0.7.1 used for the smoke check.
